pivotal_result: EPOCH, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled 78-week trial in 1958 patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer disease: the mean change in ADAS-cog score was 7.9 points with verubecestat 12 mg and 8.0 points with 40 mg, versus 7.7 points with placebo (P = 0.63 and P = 0.46 respectively), and ADCS-ADL changes likewise did not differ significantly; the trial was terminated early for futility, and the authors concluded that verubecestat did not reduce cognitive or functional decline. Adverse events including rash, falls and injuries, sleep disturbance, suicidal ideation, weight loss and hair-color change were more common with verubecestat. Trial registration NCT01739348; paper DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1706441.
reason_class: Failed primary endpoints; trial terminated early for futility
